The deploy surface renders no antd Menu, Popover or Dropdown: a search of ui/src/pages/deploy and ui/src/pages/DeployPage.tsx finds none of those components, so the floating layers this item is about are the antd Select overlays, which are the only layers that open and close on the page. Each of the three assertions is a measurement. First, the trigger carries an accessible name where the product gives it one, and the vendor overlay opens from the mouse with real rows to choose (two rows measured). Second, the same overlay opens from the keyboard alone: focusing the trigger and pressing ArrowDown produces the same two rows, which is the keyboard operation this item asks for. Third, closing returns focus to the trigger, asserted by reading document.activeElement's class rather than by assuming it. The disabled case is a real object on this page: the node picker carries aria-label 'Only these nodes' and sits inside .ant-select-disabled while node selection is automatic, and clicking it with force (bypassing the pointer guard) opens no overlay - the overlay count is 0 before and 0 after, so the disabled trigger cannot be operated. Measured values: mouse_open_rows=2, keyboard_open_rows=2, keyboard_focus_returned=true, disabled_triggers=['Only these nodes'], overlays_after_disabled_click=0. The overlay measured here is the antd Select dropdown, not a Menu: a search of ui/src/pages/deploy finds no Menu, Popover or Dropdown component, so the trigger is a combobox and its options are listbox options rather than menu items. The item's requirements are applied to that real overlay rather than to a menu that does not exist on this surface. Covered in both locales by the run ids recorded in the case report. Not mutation-proven: the behaviour is measured on the real overlays, but no product code was broken to watch these measurements fail.

The overlay is measured against the viewport and against the control that opened it, rather than being assumed to fit. With the vendor overlay open at 1440x900, every rendered row is required to lie inside the viewport on all four edges - measured two rows, both inside. The overlay is also required not to cover its own trigger: the trigger's bounding box is compared against every row's box, and no row intersects it, so the overlay cannot bury the control the operator just used. Closing the overlay is required to return focus to the trigger, asserted by reading document.activeElement rather than by assuming it, and measured true for both the keyboard close and the pointer close. Measured values: rows=2, rows_inside_viewport=2, overlay_covers_trigger=false, focus_returned=true. The overlay measured here is the antd Select dropdown, not a Menu: a search of ui/src/pages/deploy finds no Menu, Popover or Dropdown component, so the trigger is a combobox and its options are listbox options rather than menu items. The item's requirements are applied to that real overlay rather than to a menu that does not exist on this surface. The long-list end row is limited by this fixture, which supplies two vendor rows rather than a long list, and that limit is stated here instead of being glossed: the viewport-freedom assertion runs on the rows that exist. Not mutation-proven: the refusal is the product's own, so there is nothing to break in order to observe it.

A deep link naming a deployment that does not exist is required to say so rather than render a blank form or sit in its loading state; measured, it renders the result page and no element carries aria-busy=true. That landing shows the generic 'could not be opened' wording, and this case records that as a product gap instead of asserting it as correct: the API answers 404 with a body carrying only {"error": "not found"} and no code because writeErr at internal/server/api/api.go:1010-1020 adds a code only for a ProductError, so the client's parseError returns a plain Error rather than an APIError at ui/src/apiError.ts:83-84 and the not-found branch at ui/src/pages/DeployPage.tsx:81 cannot be reached. The refusal to offer a blank form is what is claimed here. Covered in both locales by the run ids recorded in the case report. Not mutation-proven.

The Expert view's tabs are switched and the result is required to stay self-consistent. The Expert view is reached through the product's own Segmented control (ui/src/pages/DeployPage.tsx:377) and renders four tabs measured by name: Model and Context, Performance, Resource Configuration, Runtime Environment (antd Tabs at ui/src/pages/deploy/DeployExpertTabs.tsx:76). After each switch exactly one tab is required to claim selection and its label is required to equal the tab that was clicked, and at least one tab panel is required to be present - so the page content and the selected tab cannot disagree. The URL relationship is measured rather than assumed: this page keeps the active tab in component state, so a switch leaves the URL unchanged and no tab or step parameter appears; the case asserts that a tab parameter, if present, agrees with the selected tab, and records that here none is present. Measured: four tabs, switches to Performance and Resource Configuration each left exactly one selected tab matching the clicked label with panels>=1 and no tab parameter in the URL. Browser back and forward are outside this page's contract because no navigation is pushed, and that is stated rather than tested. Covered in both locales by the run ids recorded in the case report. Not mutation-proven.

N/A, in three separate layers so what exists and what is reachable are not confused. First, the product has one role and cannot produce a second one to compare against: the only write of Role in the server is the literal "admin" at internal/server/store/auth.go:31 inside EnsureAdmin, which is the single creation path and takes no role argument, so no user-scoped account exists to sign in as. Second, a real administrator-only refusal does exist in the code - requireManagementAdmin at internal/server/api/auth.go:236-247 answers 403 ErrorAdministratorRequired when the claims' Role is not admin - and it is unreachable from anything this case can hold, because the claims are signed by the server and obtaining a non-admin signature would require the master key. Third, this case does not forge such a token to demonstrate it: a hand-signed credential would prove nothing about the product's own authorization and would be fabricated evidence. What this contract does prove about authorization is recorded under 13.3, where the product's real read/write platform-token split is exercised and a read token is refused a write with 403 PLATFORM_TOKEN_READ_ONLY. The admin/user menu and button comparison this item describes is not claimed.

A page path the product has no route for and an API path it has no handler for are required to be answered differently, so a bad deep link cannot be hidden behind a 200. Requested over a raw transport rather than the JSON helper, a page path with no matching route answers 200 with the SPA shell (content-type text/html and a doctype in the body), while an API path with no matching handler answers 404 with application/json and no shell markup - measured exactly that way, so the shell does not swallow the API. This is the product's real fallback behaviour: /deploy and /deploy?model=1 are served the same shell as /no-such-deploy-page, and /api/v1/definitely-not-a-route is answered by the API's own 404 rather than by the SPA document. Measured values: unrouted_page status=200 content-type=text/html, unrouted_api status=404 content-type=application/json, spa_swallows_api=false. Covered in both locales by the run ids recorded in the case report. Not mutation-proven.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-mount-readonly-default-checked
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the mount-seed oracle: the added mount row is created with read_only: true, so _append_mount's expect(checkbox).not_to_be_checked() fails inside the seeded-wire step ("Locator expected not to be checked / Actual value: checked", 9 polls resolving the real #container_mount_rows_0_read_only input). The mutated behaviour is the product default of a newly added mount row, exactly what the 6.5 seeded draft asserts.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-mount-delete-first-row-x
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the original-restored evaluate-wire oracle in the overrides context: remove(0) deletes the first original row instead of the owned pending row, so the restored draft sent for evaluate carries [override-rw, e2e-...-weights] while the contract expects [override-ro, override-rw]. The diff is visible field by field in the recorded expected/actual bodies, so the kill is the byte-exact draft-restoration assertion rather than any UI timeout.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-tristate-change-swallowed-x
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the seeded evaluate-wire byte comparison after the mutation was retargeted to the component that actually writes the quick-surface tri-state: with DeployFeatureChoice onChange reduced to a no-op, the seeded draft reaches the wire as enable_cache_report=true and enable_prefix_caching=null, while the contract requires false and true. Both differing keys are reported in the same assertion, so the failure is the tri-state seeding path and nothing else.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-create-failure-silent
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the rejection-notice oracle: the catch path shows the success message text instead of the server detail, so the error toast carrying the exact FIELD_INVALID detail never appears (".ant-message-error" filtered by the 256-character detail resolves to 0 elements across the 12s expectation window, actual value 0). This proves the 6.5 rejection notice is asserted on real product copy and not merely on the presence of any toast.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-name-length-check-removed
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the rejected-wire oracle on a real Go mutation: with the rune-count maximum removed from validateTextField the 257-rune name is accepted, so the create returns 201 where the contract requires 400 ("AssertionError: overlong name HTTP 201" at deployment_wizard_create.py:213). The mutant is a single-file Go change rebuilt into its own binary; the normal binary is untouched.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-stale-provider-accepted
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the acquisition refusal oracle on a real Go mutation: returning nil instead of ErrorAcquisitionCandidateStale lets the expired weight provider through, so the stale submit answers 201 where the contract requires 400 ("expired selected provider HTTP: expected=400; actual=201"). This is the second independent proof that the retained draft is evaluated against live provider state.

fault_runs.name: boolrej-evaluate-on-stale-error
fault_runs.review_note: Killed by the expiry guard: injecting a real api.evaluate({}) into the catch path makes the client emit evaluate traffic while the selected provider is expired, so the guard's "requests" list is non-empty and "6.5 mode/read observations emitted evaluate while provider expired" fails at the retained mount read-only expert step. The observation is recorded by a request guard rather than inferred from the UI.
